structure.overview: Ms. Luttrell sought judicial review of a refusal to grant her a Temporary Resident Permit (TRP) after her permanent residence application was denied. The Minister argued the review was moot because Ms. Luttrell had since been granted a valid TRP. The Federal Court agreed the review was moot and dismissed the application without considering the merits.

sections.label: Issue of mootness and judicial discretion

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell argues the Officer erred by applying the wrong standard, misassessing her immigration history, and misjudging the child's best interest.
idea_list: Error in best interest of child assessment

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Minister contends the judicial review is moot because Ms. Luttrell was granted a one-year TRP in December 2024.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court agrees the review is moot due to the valid TRP and declines to consider the matter on merits.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell's 2021 permanent residence application on humanitarian grounds was refused, and judicial review was dismissed.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell applied for a TRP in February 2022 citing no criminal record, family ties, work with disabled children, and community advocacy.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: In August 2023, the officer upheld the TRP refusal, citing lack of exceptional circumstances and Ms. Luttrell's ability to regularize status otherwise.

summaries.speaker: evidence
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell applied for an open work permit on January 23, 2025, which remains under processing.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell argues the review is not moot due to future TRP needs and urges the Court to exercise discretion to hear the matter.
idea_list: Future TRP need keeps controversy alive
Collateral consequences and judicial economy arguments

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court rejects Ms. Luttrell's arguments and finds the application moot.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court agrees no live controversy exists as Ms. Luttrell holds a valid TRP, so judicial review would have no practical effect.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court finds Ms. Luttrell's possible future TRP need speculative and insufficient to maintain a live controversy.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court finds no adversarial context remains since Ms. Luttrell was granted a TRP and the Minister's arguments were brief.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court finds no collateral consequences exist as TRP decisions are discretionary and fact-specific, limiting precedential value.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Judicial economy favors dismissal as the case has no practical effect and existing case law addresses TRP standards.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Judicial resources already spent make judicial economy a neutral factor in deciding whether to hear the case.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court notes no question of general importance arises and Ms. Luttrell made no submissions on the law-making function factor.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court concludes the Borowski test and interests of justice weigh against hearing Ms. Luttrell's judicial review application.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The parties did not propose any question of general importance for certification.
